claims.statement: Kissaten models coffee origin as a three-level hierarchy: Country (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code) → Region (sub-national admin area) → Farm (specific production site), with the Bean Pydantic model capturing all three plus producer, elevation_min/max, latitude/longitude, process, variety, and cost-transparency fields.

A CoffeeBean carries an origins list (array) rather than a single origin, so blends can list each constituent origin/lot independently; the origins field cannot be updated via diffjson and requires a full bean JSON file.

The origins DuckDB table stores raw scraped values plus pre-computed normalised/canonical columns (region_normalized, farm_normalized, state_canonical, state_canonical_slug, farm_canonical) used for deduplication and querying, with a foreign key bean_id referencing coffee_beans.id.

The normalisation helpers (normalize_region_name, normalize_farm_name, normalize_process_name, normalize_varietal_name) follow the same recipe: Unicode NFKD decomposition, drop non-ASCII diacritics, lowercase, keep alphanumerics/spaces/hyphens, collapse runs to single hyphens; they are registered as DuckDB UDFs.

The region_mappings directory holds 48 country JSON files keyed by raw region strings, each resolving to a canonical_state plus full geocoding metadata; load_region_mappings reads them into _region_mappings at startup keyed by upper-cased country code.

get_canonical_state(country_code, region_name) looks up the region_mappings for a country and returns the canonical_state (or None for explicitly invalid/failed regions, preserving NULL), falling back to the original region name when no mapping exists; during load each origins row is backfilled with state_canonical and state_canonical_slug.

The geocoding pipeline uses OpenCageGeocoder (services/geocoding.py) which queries the OpenCage API with region + ISO country code, caches full responses to data/geocoding_cache/{CC}/{normalized}.json, retries HTTP 429 with exponential backoff, and extracts the state name with priority state → state_district → province → county; scripts/deduplicate_regions.py drives it and writes region_mappings/{CC}.json.

The canonical region-slug grouping invariant requires every region endpoint to identify a region by the effective slug expression COALESCE(normalize_region_name(o.state_canonical), o.region_normalized) — implemented as COALESCE(o.state_canonical_slug, o.region_normalized) — so multiple raw regions mapping to one canonical state collapse into a single entry (e.g. Boquete and Volcán both become chiriqui).

An OR-based region filter (normalize_region_name(state_canonical) = ? OR region_normalized = ?) causes slug leaks: e.g. querying sidama-bensa returned 55 beans instead of 7 because rows whose raw slug matched but whose canonical slug belonged to a different group were incorrectly included; the COALESCE-based filter evaluates each row's effective slug once and avoids the leak.

Region-detail's six sub-queries (stats, known farms, unknown farms, varietals, processes, elevation) that re-join origins on bean_id must all re-apply the region filter (AND {region_filter_sql}); omitting it on even one join leaks data from other regions into the response because a bean can have origins in multiple regions.

Farm counts use COUNT(DISTINCT COALESCE(o.farm_canonical, o.farm_normalized)) FILTER (WHERE o.farm IS NOT NULL AND o.farm != '') consistently in list and detail endpoints; farm_normalized is the COALESCE fallback for stable deduplication and the FILTER excludes unnamed farms, so the synthetic Unknown Farm bucket is not counted in farm_count/total_farms.

The /v1/origins API forms a strict hierarchy: GET /v1/origins (country list, GROUP BY country), GET /v1/origins/{country_code} (CountryDetailResponse), GET /v1/origins/{country_code}/regions (RegionSummary list grouped by canonical slug), GET /v1/origins/{country_code}/{region_slug} (RegionDetailResponse), GET /v1/origins/{country_code}/{region_slug}/{farm_slug} (FarmDetailResponse); all are cached with SimpleMemoryCache.

Country/region/farm codes are normalised on entry (country_code.upper(), region_slug.lower(), farm_slug.lower()); the special slugs unknown-region and unknown-farm match rows where region/farm is NULL or empty, keeping beans with missing origin data reachable.

Country/region/farm detail endpoints materialise a per-request temporary table (_country_beans_, _region_beans_, _farm_beans_) from the single slow scan, run all subsequent aggregation queries against it, and drop it in a finally block; display names prefer MODE(state_canonical) FILTER falling back to MODE(region).

Elevation is captured as a per-origin elevation_min/elevation_max range (0-3000 m, 0 meaning not known) and aggregated at every hierarchy level: country detail returns avg_elevation and elevation_distribution, region list returns median_elevation, region detail returns elevation_range, and farm detail returns elevation_min/elevation_max.

latitude and longitude are optional per-origin fields constrained to valid ranges and marked 'Do not guess. If not present, return None.' because an incorrect coordinate is worse than a missing one; at farm-detail they are averaged across the farm's origin rows and returned as the farm's latitude/longitude.

The geography response models (CountryDetailResponse, RegionDetailResponse, FarmDetailResponse, RegionSummary, FarmSummary, ElevationInfo) in schemas/geography_models.py define the typed/validated structures returned by the /v1/origins hierarchy, including is_geocoded flags and elevation aggregates.

The frontend origins route mirrors the API hierarchy as a SvelteKit tree under frontend/src/routes/(main)/origins/ with GeographyBreadcrumb (breadcrumb up the hierarchy), ElevationMountainChart (elevation visualisation), UniversalOriginSearch (unified country/region/farm search), and InsightCard sections for varietals/processes/notes on all three detail pages.

The test suite enforces cross-level consistency invariants: country list↔detail counts match, region list↔detail bean/farm counts match, no duplicate region names, name round-trip, no region exceeds country, farm list matches stats, canonical slug exclusivity (subsumed raw slugs not independently addressable), and no slug leak; covered by test_origin_hierarchy_counts.py, test_region_name_consistency.py, test_canonical_slug_grouping.py, test_origins_api.py, and test_invalid_regions.py.

The frontend implements parallel normalisation (normalizeRegionName, normalizeFarmName in frontend/src/lib/utils.ts) so URL slugs it generates for breadcrumbs and links match the slugs the backend expects.
